problem:
Which of the following equalities are true given that
$D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 2,\,\frac{1}{2}\le y\le 1}.$

- ${∬}_{D}y\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}A={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{1/2}^{1}y\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$
- ${∬}_{D}y\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}A={\int }_{1/2}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}y\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$
- ${∬}_{D}y\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\text{d}A={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{1/2}^{1}y\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant. 

Making a substitution $xy=u,$ $\text{d}y=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}u,$ we get.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}x{e}^{xy}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x[{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{xy}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x[{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{1}{x}{e}^{u}\,\text{d}u]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{x}{e}^{u}\,\text{d}u]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{e}^{u}]_{0}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{x}-1)\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{x}-1)\,\text{d}x & =[{e}^{x}-x]_{0}^{1} \\  & =(e-1)-(1-0) \\  & =e-2\end{aligned}
$$
